subject: Using integrate_ode_cvode for a PKPD model gives an error?

messages.author: 25ce5e85187da1a3
messages.subject: Using integrate_ode_cvode for a PKPD model gives an error?
parts:
Hi Stan experts,

I am trying implement different PKPD models using "integrate_ode_cvode" function with cmdstan development version. I started the simple scenarios as given here https://groups.google.com/forum/#!category-topic/stan-users/general/LgjBmbAjU1E
As you suggested in the manual, I am adding more complexity to the models step by step. My aim is Stan implementation of a K-PD model which is introduced in this paper http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/17051439
With this K-PD model, the scenarios of "single dosing regime with n patients" and "multiple dosing regime with one patient" worked very nicely. However the "multiple doses with n patients" scenario gave me the attached error after running it almost 3 days.
By the way, I am simulating dataset with Stan and then trying to estimate them.

I used "integrated_ode_cvode" as explained here by Michael Betancourt answer https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/stan-users/AkzvXZPSv6M/tBEu9pLDAAAJ.

And my problem is similar as answered here https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/stan-users/ODE/stan-users/3Qdxnizb-B4/tGXOwcWpAAAJ. After I increased the max_num_steps from 1e8 to 1e10, I got the same error (my init is already 0.25). And also I looked
the Section B.2 of the CVODE manual, but I did not understand how to solve my issue.

I think that it is an ODE integrator problem, can you help me about this problem, what can I do to make it work? Should I change the Stan model?

I attached Stan codes of my working examples. And the example that giving error and its dump data format and the corresponding cmdstan error.

I am using cmdstan development version which I updated last week.

My call to stan is: PK_PD_models/PKPD_Mdose_npats/PKPD_Mdose_npats random seed=225 sample algorithm=hmc stepsize=0.001 data file=PK_PD_models/PKPD_Mdose_npats/PKPD_Mdose_npats.data.R  init=0.25

My operating system is Linux and g++ version is below:

g++ --v
Using built-in specs.
Target: x86_64-redhat-linux
Configured with: ../configure --prefix=/usr --mandir=/usr/share/man --infodir=/usr/share/info --with-bugurl=http://bugzilla.redhat.com/bugzilla --enable-bootstrap --enable-shared --enable-threads=posix --enable-checking=release --with-system-zlib --enable-__cxa_atexit --disable-libunwind-exceptions --enable-gnu-unique-object --enable-languages=c,c++,objc,obj-c++,java,fortran,ada --enable-java-awt=gtk --disable-dssi --with-java-home=/usr/lib/jvm/java-1.5.0-gcj-1.5.0.0/jre --enable-libgcj-multifile --enable-java-maintainer-mode --with-ecj-jar=/usr/share/java/eclipse-ecj.jar --disable-libjava-multilib --with-ppl --with-cloog --with-tune=generic --with-arch_32=i686 --build=x86_64-redhat-linux
Thread model: posix
gcc version 4.4.6 20120305 (Red Hat 4.4.6-4) (GCC)

Also, I tried on Windows, but I got the same error.

Thank you very much for your help and any suggestions,

Burak Kursad Gunhan

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: Using integrate_ode_cvode for a PKPD model gives an error?
parts:
Hi!

Have you tried running the model with the RK45 integrate_ode function? These PK/PD (or K-PD) problems run most of the time quite well with the non-stiff RK45 (and much faster) integrator.

From a very quick look at the paper I did not figure out what the response model is - just direct response, turn-over (if so which one) or effect cmt - or some combination?

Also: If the PK is analytic, you better give it in analytic form to the integrator...

Sebastian

messages.subject: Re: Using integrate_ode_cvode for a PKPD model gives an error?
parts:
Hi Sebastian,

Thank you very much for your reply.

Yes, I have tried RK45 integrate_ode function. For even simpler models, it was get stuck, and was not continuing simulations, thats why I switch to new ODE integrator.

This is an indirect response model. For the PK part, it uses a one-compartment model.

Yes, the PK part is analytic, maybe I should use analytical solution of the PK part. But, is it possible to use PK part as analytic and solving only the second ODE (which is more complicated)? I could not manage to implement this in Stan?

Again thanks for any help,

Burak
